title: Will Tidö parties win a majority in the 2026 Swedish parliamentary elections?
description:
In October 2022, the Swedish political parties Sweden Democrats (SD), Moderate Party (M), Christian Democrats (KD), and Liberals (L) signed the Tidö Agreement (Tidöavtalet) to form a government after the 2022 Swedish parliamentary elections.

Parliamentary elections are scheduled to be held in Sweden on September 13, 2026. This market will resolve to “Yes” if the member parties of the Tidö Agreement (SD, M, KD, and L) win a combined total of 175 seats or more in the 2026 Swedish parliamentary elections. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If voting in the 2026 Swedish parliamentary elections does not occur by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named parties in the Swedish Parliament (Riksdag). 

This market will resolve based on the results of this election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Swedish government, specifically the Swedish Election Authority (Valmyndigheten) (https://www.val.se/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent opinion polls indicate the Tidö bloc—Moderates, Christian Democrats and Liberals with Sweden Democrats support—trails the opposition Red-Green parties by roughly 10–12 points, translating to projected seat shares below the 175-seat majority threshold. Multiple surveys from May 2026, including those by SCB, Ipsos and Demoskop, place the governing side at 42–44 percent while the centre-left reaches 52–55 percent. The gap has persisted through spring, with voters citing economic pressures, unemployment and living costs. In response, the government recently adjusted planned deportation rules for young adults, reflecting electoral calculations ahead of the September 13 vote. These trends underpin trader expectations that the current coalition partners will fall short of an outright majority.
